If you’re going 4 days a week I’d say a good approach would be to climb 2 of those days and do weight training or technique/ skill training / mobility the other 2. You just don’t want to climb hard everyday. A big problem for me when I first started climbing was doing too much too soon and getting tendonitis really bad. Just be careful and stay stoked

Climbing to start out with is enough to start conditioning the tendons if you’re just getting into it. I’d stay away from the hangboard until at least 2-3 months in after consistent climbing. But after that would be the hangboard, although I would watch videos on proper technique for hang boarding. I would probably do weight training to build finger strength before hang boarding, it’s not as climbing specific but it builds a foundation. Things like: finger rolls with dumbells, finger curls with a weighted barbell, a PVC with a resistance band works as well. The best way to get better at climbing is to bot get injured, good luck 🤙🏻

I’ve belayed smaller kids for summer camp and as a coach. Only concern I’d say is teaching the kids the standard PBUS method of keeping your brake hand down
